t5760.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Muḥammad ibn Bakr ibn ʿUthmān al-Bursānī, Abū ʿUthmān al-Baṣrī, as truthful but may err (ṣadūq qad yukhṭiʾ) from the ninth generation; he died in 204 AH.
as: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
By God, he was refined and well-mannered.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
محمد بن عبد الله بن عمار الموصلي, quoted by al-Mizzī
لم يكن صاحب حديث، تركناه لم نسمع منه.
He was not a hadith specialist. We passed him over and did not hear from him.
الحافظ أبو بكر الخطيب, quoted by al-Mizzī
يعني إنه لم يكن كغيره من الحفاظ في وقته وهم: حيي بن سعيد القطان، وعبد الرحمن ابن مهدي واشباههما.
He meant that al-Bursānī was not at the level of the leading hadith masters of his time, such as al-Qaṭṭān and Ibn Mahdī.
Ibn Ḥibbān listed him in The Reliable Transmitters.

t880.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Jābir or Juwaybir al-ʿAbdī as acceptable (maqbūl) and belonging to the third generation.

t8815.bio: Ibn Ḥajar identifies Ibn Judʿān as ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muḥammad ibn Judʿān, who transmitted from his unknown grandmother, from Umm Salamah; she is of the third generation.

uthba.bio: A Medinan jurist. Ibn Ḥajar records 94 AH, 98 AH and other reports for his death.
as: Trustworthy, a jurist and firm in transmission.
Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
Reliable, trustworthy, and a leading authority.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
Asked whether ʿIkrimah or ʿUbayd Allāh was preferable from Ibn ʿAbbās: both, without preferring either.
كان عالما وقد ذهب بصره وكان ثقة فقيها كثير الحديث والعلم شاعرا
He was a scholar who had lost his sight; trustworthy, a jurist, with much hadith and knowledge, and a poet.
تابعي ثقة، رجل صالح، جامع للعلم وهو معلم عمر بن عبد العزيز
A trustworthy Successor, a righteous man, comprehensive in knowledge, and teacher of ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz.
فإنه لم آته إلا وجدت عنده علما طريفا
Whenever I came to him I found fresh knowledge with him.
كان عبيد الله عالما وكان قد ذهب بصره
ʿUbayd Allāh was a scholar and had lost his sight.
